messages:
maya: heads up: seeing mass OOMs from continuous-batcher in us-east-1 (cb-us-east). latency p95 for /v1/chat/generate spiked from 1.8s -> 12s, errors ~6%. pods restarting, nodes showing GPU page faults. grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/CB/continuous-batcher-us-east

incident-bot: NEW INCIDENT INC-2026-3412350001 | severity: P1 | channels: #eng-oncall, #incidents | responder: eng-oncall

jordan: ack. any deploys in last hour? which model variants?

maya: deploy-bot pushed rollout 9a3b2e last 18m by CI. env diff shows `BATCHER_PREFETCH_FACTOR=64` (used to be 4). suspect prefetch/accumulator amplification. grabbing logs now.

maya: ```
kubectl logs -n runtime cb-batcher-2d9c
[2026-03-16T02:14:10Z] WARN prefetch: prefetch_queue=85000
[2026-03-16T02:14:11Z] ERROR runtime: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation when allocating KV cache 128MB
[2026-03-16T02:14:11Z] ERROR container runtime: process exited with status 137
[2026-03-16T02:14:12Z] INFO accumulator: outstanding_requests=92012
```

deploy-bot: Rollout 9a3b2e -> paused. Diff: BATCHER_PREFETCH_FACTOR=64 (was 4)

lee: that env is dangerous for memory blowup if combined with sticky-kv cache. was there a config change to kv retention?

maya: yes, model redwood-32b-kv-retain=true rolled as part of the same deploy. combined effect = many requests holding onto large caches + aggressive prefetch.

sam: mitigation plan (short): 1) pause rollout (done), 2) hotpatch deploy to reset BATCHER_PREFETCH_FACTOR=4, 3) enable immediate kv eviction for pool, 4) put routing backpressure: temporarily limit requests per-second to cb-us-east, 5) cordon hottest nodes, evict and restart pods.

jordan: applying hotpatch: `kubectl set env deployment/cb-batcher BATCHER_PREFETCH_FACTOR=4 -n runtime`

jordan: also toggling runtime flag `--kv-evict-immediately=true` on the deployment template (will restart pods).

ops-bot: node ip-10-1-14-203 cordoned due to repeated GPU page faults.

maya: redeployed with hotpatch. new pods initializing. watching logs.

maya: new pod logs show prefetch queue back to normal.

maya: ```
[2026-03-16T02:22:04Z] INFO prefetch: prefetch_queue=3120
[2026-03-16T02:22:05Z] INFO health: kv_evictions=active
[2026-03-16T02:22:05Z] INFO latency: p95=2.1s
```

natalie: customer impact check: which tenants hit errors? support shows spikes from dedicated pools C and D. listing: T-201, T-402, T-777. T-402 saw 8% 429s for ~18m.

jordan: applying route-level throttle in API gateway to cb-us-east: `limit requests 1000/s -> 300/s` for emergency.

sam: also enabling per-tenant backpressure to protect large tenants while we stabilize.

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-3412350001 acknowledged by on-call jordan. escalation timer paused.

maya: latency trending down but one node still flapping. I'll keep it cordoned and request hardware diag.

lee: root cause notes so far: 1) CI/rollout changed two risky settings in one roll (prefetch + kv retention), 2) no node-level hard cap to prevent accumulator/prefetch runaway, 3) alerts for prefetch_queue growth were insufficient (threshold set too high).

sam: short-term done: rollback/hotpatch, kv eviction enabled, gateway throttle, cordon nodes, restart flapped nodes.

jordan: medium-term actions: enforce CI safety rule to block combined changes to PREFETCH_FACTOR and KV_RETENTION in same rollout without ops approval; add node-level OOM quarantine that evicts offending containers before node OOM; add alert: prefetch_queue > 20k triggers paging page and PD P1; add automated rollback when >=3 OOMKills in 5m across a deployment.

natalie: sending inbound customer comms: initial notice + mitigation timeline. offering account credits for T-402 and T-777.

maya: impact summary: incident window 02:13-02:32 UTC. estimated SLO blip: p95 increase from 1.8s->12s for us-east for ~19 minutes; affected tenants ~0.6% of total generation traffic in region, targeted dedicated tenants T-201/T-402/T-777 saw elevated errors.

lee: add to postmortem owner list: owner @lee, tech lead @sam, oncall @jordan, comms @natalie. deliverable: postmortem + runbook update by EOD.

jordan: handing off monitoring to @sam. I'll pair for 20m and then sign off.

sam: taking over. keeping gateway throttle and kv eviction for 30m, then we'll relax if stable.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE INC-2026-3412350001 severity downgraded to P2 1:02 UTC 1:40 UTC: conditions stabilizing.

ops-bot: uploaded `nvidia-smi` and dmesg output from flapped nodes to incident artifact store.

maya: thanks all. will collate logs and open postmortem. final note: add automated lint for risky env vars in deploy-diffs (PREFETCH_FACTOR > 16 triggers blocker).

natalie: comms queued. will follow up with customers with final postmortem link once ready.

sam: leaving gateway throttle in place for now. will relax incrementally if no regressions.

jordan: handoff complete. monitoring window started.

maya: incident closed in PD when monitoring window passed. converting thread to draft postmortem. closing Slack thread.
